title: Privacy-sensitive embeddings & fallback hosting options - discovery
summary: Initial discovery for CaroHealth's privacy-sensitive embeddings pilot. Main concerns: where to host embeddings (hosted vs dedicated vs private), KMS/encryption and auditability, vector DB integration path, throughput and embedding dimensionality tradeoffs, and a fallback/hybrid search model for availability and cost. Agreed next step: Redwood to run a small throughput benchmark plan and share security artifacts; customer to provide sample dataset and queries.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-03 16:00 PT | Duration ~48m | Attendees: Alex Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood solutions), Dana Kim (CaroHealth Head of Search), Mark Liu (Platform), Isabel Torres (CTO)

Summary (auto): discuss hosting and privacy constraints, integration plan for vector DB, throughput targets (p50/p95), and pilot success criteria.

[00:00] Alex M: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, i'm alex, i'm the account lead at Redwood. priya and jordan from our side will cover architecture and the benchmark plan. dana, isabel, mark, thanks for joining.
[00:12] Dana K: thanks, alex. yeah, we want to kick off by laying out constraints — PHI-ish data, need strict controls, also latency targets for search within our clinician UI.
[00:22] Priya S: absolutely, thanks. can you remind us of the throughput and latency targets you care about? you mentioned bursty during rounds and steady during daytime?
[00:34] Mark L: yeah, roughly 200 qps during clinic hours, but spikes to 800 qps for batch scoring after dedupe jobs. latency for interactive use should be under 200ms p50 ideally, p95 < 600ms is tolerable.
[00:47] Isabel T: and on privacy, we need data never to leave our VPC for identifiable content; disk encryption + bring-your-own-KMS, and audit logs for every request are mandatory. SOC2 type 2 is required and SSO integration (SAML).
[01:05] Alex M: good to call those out. we support three modes — hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC / on-prem). for PHI we usually see customers run private or dedicated with strict routing, but we can discuss nuances.
[01:22] Dana K: ok, technical question: we currently store vectors in a managed vector DB (weaviate) in our cloud account. do you prefer we keep vectors there or use redwood embeddings + host vectors in your infra?
[01:34] Priya S: short answer: either. common pattern is embeddings generated by Redwood hosted API and pushed to customer's vector DB. For private hosting, Redwood can run inference in your VPC so embeddings never cross the internet. if you need dedicated GPU pools, we can do a dedicated setup but the vectors remain in your db.
[01:53] Mark L: how does caching work with the KV stuff? and i'm hearing 'KV cache' but sometimes transcripts say K V cash (laugh) — how does prefix caching behave for rerank flows?
[02:05] Jordan L: good question — runtime uses prefix/KV cache to avoid redoing decoder work for repeated prefixes in chat, for embeddings pipelines it's about batching and reusing encoded chunks. for rerank we recommend local re-ranking on the app layer if possible or a short-lived cache on the inference side.
[02:25] Dana K: our re-rank path is: user query -> vector DB topk -> then LLM rerank returned candidates. that's where latency tightness is. we're evaluating doing 128-dim vs 512-dim embeddings to trade cost vs accuracy. any guidance?
[02:38] Priya S: we ran a bunch of evals — 128 dim can be fine for coarse recall but you'll likely lose fine-grain relevance; 512 or 768 tends to perform better for rerank downstream. cost scales with tokenization and throughput but more importantly with index size and fanout. if you have a high fanout (topk 200+) you will see latency/cost grow.
[02:58] Mark L: so practical question: if we keep vectors in weaviate, who runs the rerank model? we want rerank inside our VPC to avoid moving candidate content out.
[03:10] Priya S: with private deployment we can spin up an inference tier in your VPC that calls your weaviate over internal network, does the rerank, and returns scores. or, with dedicated, we can set up secure peering and private endpoints. both support BYOK KMS for disk and model artifacts.
[03:28] Isabel T: audit trails — can you produce per-request logs with user ids and token counts? need to keep them for 1 year.
[03:35] Alex M: yes, audit logs with request metadata, token counts, and model version are standard on our enterprise packages. retention is configurable — we can tie into your cloud logging bucket or deliver via secure SFTP.
[03:50] Dana K: what's the fallback story? if dedicated pool is saturated, do you autoscale or do we hit a queued state and fail open to a cheaper model?
[04:00] Jordan L: we have smart routing — policies can route to cheaper quantized variants or to a hosted fall-back region, and you can set an availability policy to prefer private/dedicated and fall back to hosted-only with data-stripping (non-PII) if you accept that risk. some customers choose canary or A/B fallbacks.
[04:20] Mark L: i want to quantify cost, priya — for 200-800 qps and topk 100 reranks, any back of envelope numbers?
[04:28] Priya S: ballpark — if you run rerank on a medium model at 512 dims and topk 100, with efficient batching you might need several gpus for steady throughput; costs vary by hosting mode. we will run a small benchmark on your sample queries to give exact GPU needs and cost estimate.
[04:45] Alex M: action: we'll propose a benchmark that simulates your fanout and spike profile. priya will outline the test matrix.
[04:52] Dana K: good. also, we use Pinecone in some projects and Milvus in others — any ops differences integrating with both?
[05:00] Priya S: integration is straightforward — we adapt connectors. main ops differences are: pinecone has managed scaling with some limits on custom shard control, milvus gives you more control if self-hosted. weaviate offers graph features some teams like. we'll include connector notes in the doc.
[05:21] Mark L: are there examples of customers with similar PHI constraints who ran private deployment?
[05:27] Jordan L: yes, we helped a telehealth startup run a VPC private deployment with BYOK. they kept vectors in their DB and inference inside VPC; we integrated KMS and SAML.
[05:42] Isabel T: how long does a private deployment typically take? we need to plan for procurement and ops windows.
[05:48] Priya S: timeline: dedicated is usually 2-4 weeks (provisioning and config), private VPC can be 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS integration. on-prem pushes further.
[06:01] Dana K: success criteria for pilot — we want to measure recall uplift vs existing embeddings, p95 latency under 600ms for interactive flows, and proof that data never leaves our control for PHI queries.
[06:16] Alex M: makes sense. we'll define an evaluation plan with those metrics.
[06:20] Mark L: on dimensionality: could you run a sweep 128/256/512 with our sample dataset?
[06:25] Priya S: yes, the benchmark will include dimension sweeps and topk variation. we'll attach a small quality eval.
[06:31] Dana K: regarding encryption — BYOK KMS, do you support Cloud HSM / external key stores?
[06:38] Alex M: we support KMS integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-managed HSMs when on private deployments. we'll share the security integration doc.
[06:49] Isabel T: regulatory question: where do logs live if you route to hosted fallback? we can't have any PHI logged in external systems even temporarily.
[06:57] Jordan L: safe default is to strip PHI before fallback or to fail closed. routing policy can be 'no fallback' for PHI routes. we can also mask or tokenise sensitive fields at the application layer before sending to Redwood hosted endpoints.
[07:12] Dana K: good — we'll likely require 'no fallback' for PHI, and maybe allow fallback for non-PHI analytics flows.
[07:18] Alex M: noted. competitive landscape: many teams use managed vector dbs plus homegrown rerank. competitors like Pinecone are vector dbs rather than full inference platform; others offer hosted-only inference without the private option.
[07:33] Mark L: we'll need pricing scenarios for three modes: hosted (strict masking), dedicated reserved (peaks of 800 qps), and private VPC.
[07:42] Priya S: we'll prepare a cost model after the benchmark.
[07:45] Dana K: any gotchas on embeddings format or normalization? we have tokens coming from multiple sources — notes, transcripts, PEC docs.
[07:54] Priya S: normalization matters — consistent preprocessing gives better recall. we'll share recommended pipelines. also watch out for heterogenous doc lengths impacting batch sizing.
[08:08] Alex M: quick runthrough of next steps and owners: priya will draft benchmark matrix; alex will send security package; mark to share sample dataset; dana to confirm stakeholders and timeline.
[08:20] Dana K: we aim to decide vendor by end of May, so tight timeline.
[08:25] Alex M: understood — we'll treat this as a prioritized pilot.
[08:30] Isabel T: final small ask — can you include a diagram showing network flow for private vs dedicated vs hosted?
[08:36] Jordan L: yes, we'll include an architecture diagram and a path for data flow showing KMS and audit log placement.
[08:44] Alex M: any other questions?
[08:47] Mark L: none from me.
[08:49] Dana K: that's it, thanks.
[08:51] Alex M: great, thanks all — we'll follow up with the benchmark plan and security docs.

End of transcript.
